summary: Post-claim validation found the allocator recovery hint stale: generation 1 had already implemented the reusable append-only create retry helper, added tests and durable evidence, and reported 5/5 passing. No substantive hot-path mutation was made by generation 2. This terminal return closes duplicate recovery without redoing completed work.
tests: POST_CLAIM_VALIDATION: prior G1 return reports reusable implementation + 5/5 passing tests.
NO_SUBSTANTIVE_MUTATION: generation 2 changed no helper, test, protocol, Current, Served or Human Accepted state.
STALE_HINT_ABORT: recovery closed by terminal NO_ACTION_NEEDED rather than duplicate implementation.
unresolved: The prior G1 return uses outcome SUCCESS, while the worker contract enumerates DONE/VERIFIED/NO_ACTION_NEEDED/SUPERSEDED as terminal. This vocabulary mismatch allowed completed work to remain allocator-recoverable.

spawn_candidates.title: Normalize completed portfolio return outcomes before allocator recovery
spawn_candidates.reason: A materially completed G1 return labeled SUCCESS was not recognized as terminal by the current portfolio contract/allocator path, causing unnecessary recovery work.
acceptance: Allocator and portfolio contract share one explicit terminal outcome vocabulary.
Historical SUCCESS returns that clearly represent completion are deterministically normalized or reconciled without replaying completed jobs.
Regression coverage proves completed jobs do not re-enter recovery solely because of outcome-label drift.
